title: Cauchy identities for skew Ferrers shapes via RSK and keys
abstract: Let $μ\subseteqλ\subseteq(m^n)$. We characterize the image under the ordinary Robinson--Schensted--Knuth correspondence of matrices supported on the skew Ferrers diagram $λ/μ$. The outer boundary determines an upper bound on the right key of the insertion tableau, while the inner boundary determines a lower bound on its left key; both bounds depend on the keys of the recording tableau. This yields tableau expansions of skew Ferrers Cauchy kernels using the standard basis polynomials of Lascoux and Schützenberger, indexed by intervals in Bruhat order. The proof first treats ordinary Ferrers diagrams. Using the supremum characterization of right keys from earlier work, we follow the $λ$-dependent bounds through single RSK insertions. When $λ$ has repeated parts, these weak column bounds need not form a semistandard tableau. Strictification determines a set $\operatorname{Comp}(λ)$ of admissible weak compositions and, for each $α\in\operatorname{Comp}(λ)$, a composition $α^λ$. Ordinary RSK then gives a weight-preserving bijective realization of the expansion \[ \prod_{(i,j)\inλ}\frac{1}{1-x_i y_j} = \sum_{α\in\operatorname{Comp}(λ)} \hat K_α(x)K_{α^λ}(y), \] where $\hat K_α$ and $K_α$ denote Demazure atoms and key polynomials, respectively. We also give a direct admissibility criterion and a parking procedure for computing $α^λ$. After translating conventions, these agree with the admissibility condition and half-bubble-sort construction of Feigin, Khoroshkin, and Makedonskyi. The staircase and truncated-staircase identities follow as special cases. Finally, we extend the weak-bound construction to an infinite alphabet, where strictification need not exist, and derive the infinite-variable Cauchy identity for the $m$-symmetric Schur functions.

title: A super Robinson–Schensted–Knuth correspondence with symmetry and the super Littlewood–Richardson rule
Novel Point Cloud Distance Metric With Adjustable Error Sensitivity and Shape Compensation
abstract: Abstract Point distance metrics such as Chamfer Distance (CD) and Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) play a key role in evaluating the quality of reconstructed point clouds and computing training loss in point cloud reconstruction. However, the metrics show their own characteristics in evaluation, stemming from differences in their sensitivity to point cloud error traits, which, in turn, causes differences in their performance of point cloud evaluation and reconstruction. In this study, we analyzed in detail the sensitivity of distance metrics to such error traits as density imbalance and point dispersion. We showed how the sensitivity difference in metrics affects their performance in point cloud evaluation and reconstruction. Recognizing that the sensitivity of a metric is correlated with the level of bijective one-to-one point correspondence embedded in the metric, we proposed a new metric, the nestedChamfer distance (NCD-n), that allows to adjust its sensitivity to error traits through the nested CD cycle, n, by which the level of bijective one-to-one point correspondence is controlled. In addition, we analyzed the effect of shape-induced point density difference on distance metrics and proposed taking shape compensation into account in metrics. Based on extensive experiments, we verified the difference of metrics in their sensitivities to error traits, the capability of the proposed NCD-n for adjusting its sensitivity effectively, and the effect of sensitivity adjustment and shape-compensation on the performance of point cloud evaluation and reconstruction.

title: Representing fine shape of local compacta by homotopy classes of ordinary maps
abstract: Fine shape, as defined by Melikhov, is an extension of the strong shape category of compacta (compact metrizable topological spaces) to all metrizable spaces, notable for being compatible with both Čech cohomology and Steenrod-Sitnikov homology. In this work we study fine shape of local compacta (locally compact separable metrizable spaces), and construct, for every local compactum $X$, a space $|X|$ unique up to a homotopy equivalence and such that fine shape classes from any locally compact metrizable space $Y$ to $X$ bijectively correspond to homotopy classes of ordinary maps from $Y$ to $|X|$. This correspondence is (contravariatly) functorial in $Y$, thus giving a representation of $Y$-dependent contravariant functor for a fixed $X$; the universal class corresponding to the identity map of $X$ is the homotopy class of a specific embedding of $X$ into $|X|$ that is a fine shape equivalence.

title: Heaps of pieces for lattice paths
abstract: We study heaps of pieces for lattice paths, which give a combinatorial visualization of lattice paths. We introduce two types of heaps: type $I$ and type $II$. A heap of type $I$ is characterized by peaks of a lattice path. We have a duality between a lattice path $μ$ and its dual $\overlineμ$ on heaps of type $I$. A heap of type $II$ for $μ$ is characterized by the skew shape between the lowest path and $μ$. We give a determinant expression for the generating function of heaps for general lattice paths, and an explicit formula for rational $(1,k)$-Dyck paths by using the inversion lemma. We introduce and study heaps in $k+1$-dimensions which are bijective to heaps of type $II$ for $(1,k)$-Dyck paths. Further, we show a bijective correspondence between type $I$ and type $II$ in the case of rational $(1,k)$-Dyck paths. As another application of heaps, we give two explicit formulae for the generating function of heaps for symmetric Dyck paths in terms of statistics on Dyck paths and on symmetric Dyck paths respectively.

title: DisPose: Disentangling Pose Guidance for Controllable Human Image Animation
abstract: Controllable human image animation aims to generate videos from reference images using driving videos. Due to the limited control signals provided by sparse guidance (e.g., skeleton pose), recent works have attempted to introduce additional dense conditions (e.g., depth map) to ensure motion alignment. However, such strict dense guidance impairs the quality of the generated video when the body shape of the reference character differs significantly from that of the driving video. In this paper, we present DisPose to mine more generalizable and effective control signals without additional dense input, which disentangles the sparse skeleton pose in human image animation into motion field guidance and keypoint correspondence. Specifically, we generate a dense motion field from a sparse motion field and the reference image, which provides region-level dense guidance while maintaining the generalization of the sparse pose control. We also extract diffusion features corresponding to pose keypoints from the reference image, and then these point features are transferred to the target pose to provide distinct identity information. To seamlessly integrate into existing models, we propose a plug-and-play hybrid ControlNet that improves the quality and consistency of generated videos while freezing the existing model parameters. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate the superiority of DisPose compared to current methods. Project page: \href{https://github.com/lihxxx/DisPose}{https://github.com/lihxxx/DisPose}.

title: Constructivismo en el análisis de las relaciones entre China y América Latina: Una mirada desde las perspectivas wentianas
abstract: In this critical analysis, the Sino-Latin American relationship is approached from the constructivist perspective, challenging the materialistic approaches that have predominated in studies on this topic. Constructivism seeks to explore aspects underestimated by materialistic discourses and open new dimensions of analysis in the international relations between China and Latin America. Traditionally, the focus of foreign relations has been on historical categories and theories such as neoliberalism and dependency theory. However, constructivism aims to understand a new international culture that transcends the material, incorporating cultural and ideational aspects. In this context, the article centers on the state identities of China and Latin American countries as a starting point for analyzing their international relations. It acknowledges that shared perceptions, norms, and cultural narratives are crucial in shaping states' identities and formulating their foreign policies. The cultural correspondence between the Chinese state and Latin America is explored through the analysis of Wendt's "cultural structures" in the international system: the Hobbesian, Lockean, and Kantian cultures. This exploration allows an understanding of the current cultural logic among actors in the international system. It is crucial to highlight the United States' influence in the international system and its relationship with China and Latin American countries. This approach emphasizes the complexities and contrasts in Sino-American and Latin American-United States relations, framing them within the dynamics of the Lockean logic that characterizes the global structure of the international system. Understanding the cultural and ideational dimensions of these international interactions provides a more comprehensive view of relationships and contributes to a deeper understanding of how these cultural dynamics shape states' identities and decisions in the international system. Constructivism emerges as a valuable theoretical framework to enrich the analysis of international relations and open new perspectives in the study of interactions between China and Latin America.

title: ASM-6D: Fast Certified Pose-Shape Inference with Complete Correspondence Flow Maps
abstract: Category-level 6D pose and shape estimation requires recovering an object's pose and geometry from partial observations without an exact instance model. We present ASM-6D, which couples generative complete-geometry prediction with explicit category-level pose-shape inference through shared correspondences. Given an RGB-D image, ASM-6D generates alternative complete 3D correspondence hypotheses whose point identities are shared with a category-level Active Shape Model (ASM), including occluded points. Each hypothesis is fitted directly for rotation, translation, metric scale, and instance shape without a separate correspondence-assignment stage. We analytically eliminate translation and shape coefficients, reducing fitting to a nine-variable scaled-rotation optimization problem that enables efficient batched evaluation of multiple hypotheses in real time. ASM-6D achieves state-of-the-art performance on ROPE and HouseCat6D benchmarks. Ablations demonstrate the importance of generative correspondence prediction and active shape variation. The representation also supports shape completion, shape-dependent pose ambiguity, tracking, and robotic grasping at 6-38 Hz, depending on the inference budget.

title: 自由能原理、注意力-Gibbs 桥与截断采样（Top-k/Min-P）：一个构造性机器检查视角
abstract: ## 摘要（Abstract） 本工作报告了 ConstructiveWorld 库中自由能原理（FEP）数学核、softmax 注意力与 Gibbs 分布之间的精确桥接，以及 KV 缓存逐出、top-k 截断与 Min-P 截断的构造性定量定理。全部证明在纯构造性逻辑下完成（零 Axiom、零 Admitted，仅依赖 Coq 标准库），共享同一 Cauchy 实数 / Boltzmann 分布 / KL 散度基座。核心贡献为三条主线：**(i) 温度参数化的最大熵对偶闭合（定理 4.6a–4.6e）**——对每个温度参数 t，约束熵最大化解的存在唯一性与温度-能量严格单调均被证明，核心为对称 KL 恒等 `(β1−β2)(E2−E1) == KL(p2‖p1) + KL(p1‖p2)`；**(ii) Top-k 截断的总变差（total variation, TV）精确恒等（定理 7.6，TV == tail_mass/Z_thermo）与 Min-P 截断的定量刻画（定理 8.9：dropped ≤ 1 − 1/|S|，且为熵界 dropped ≤ 1 − e^{−S} 的推论）**——截断误差的定量刻画而非仅定性记账；**(iii) 构造性 LPO 规避机制**——以弱三分 `real_weak_trich` 替代排中律、以逐 eps 余量替代“非严格且不趋近”陈述、误差累积恰为 eps（而非 |S|·eps）的归一化论证。此外，把 softmax 注意力层的迭代视为 Markov 链时的 TV 收缩与迭代收敛已在 Doeblin minorization 假设（δ ∈ (0,1)，核 ≥ δ·稳态质量）下机器检查，显式几何率 (1−δ)ⁿ：`attention_tv_contraction`、`attention_tv_iter_contraction`与 `attention_iterate_converges`全部 Qed；该簇的更一般双点形态（`u_tv_contraction` / `u_tv_iter`：免平稳性、免详细平衡、免 `transition_nonneg`、免 μ 非负，参考分布只需任意归一化）与有界 logits softmax 注意力核上的显式 Doeblin 实例化（`bs_minorization`，δ* := e^{−2Δ/T}；显式收缩率 (1 − e^{−2Δ/T})ⁿ：`bounded_softmax_tv_contraction` / `bounded_softmax_tv_iter`）亦已机器检查（见 §5.5 定理 5.4–5.6）。库内进一步在模块化扩展层闭合：温度窗口 T→∞ 半边（`temp_window_T_infty`：∀eps>0 存在 T₂>0，∀T>T₂ 时温度化权重对均匀分布的 TV ≤ eps——与 T→0 硬注意力极限构成「硬注意力–均匀混合」温度两极合龙，§5.4(a)）、KV 逐出核的有限 n 漂移界（`kv_drift_bound`：TV(K_evⁿμ, Kⁿμ) ≤ n·c + eps，∀n 有限步、无平稳性主张，§6.2.2）以及 Q/K 范数界到 双界 logits的显式转化（`qk_logits_bounded`，根有界前提形态，§5.5 定理 5.8）。支撑层包括：变分自由能分解、Gibbs 不等式与等号条件、Boltzmann 分布的自由能最小化唯一性、ELBO 下界与紧性条件、softmax 注意力即 Gibbs 分布的精确对应（单位温度、任意温度，以及缩放-温度对偶 `scale_temp_duality`：任意 c>0 下以 1/c 缩放 logits 的 softmax == 温度 c 的 softmax，把 Transformer 的 `1/√d` 缩放的 logits 层形态闭合；`√d` 覆盖已两层全闭：抽象层任意平方维数 d=k² 的见证实例化已机器检查（`sqrt_witness_nat_sq`、`scale_dual_nat_sq_k`），Real 层任意 d ≥ 0（含非平方）的构造性平方根 `real_sqrt_exists` 已证明，抽象 Id 层任意非负 d 的见证实例化亦已闭合（`sqrt_witness_exists_abstract`，模块 `UpDebtSqrtAbs`）；见 §5.4）、KV 逐出导致的稳态偏差的恒等式控制（Set 层主体为三角不等式记账，见 §6.2；另有破缺恒为零的正结果与有限 n 漂移界，见 §6.2.2；温度-Lipschitz 定量界由 Real 层定理 6.1b/6.1c 承载，见 §6.2.1）、top-k 截断的主化（majorization）最优性，以及 Min-P 截断采样的可判定性、非空性、核归一化（`minp_markov_kernel_normalized`）与相对完整 softmax 核的单调性（见 §8）。`free_energy_kl_decomp` 与 `rlhf_free_energy_kl`为同一自由能-KL 分解的两次实例化，故本工作与 RLHF/DPO 对齐目标共享同一数学基座。本文给出核心定理陈述、证明策略概述、与相关形式化工作的对比，并明确声明当前边界。**关于实例化（诚实边界）**：本文定理在实数接口 `RealInterfaceEnhanced`（Id 相等）上陈述；该接口的 setoid 对应物已由具体柯西实数端到端实例化（`Real_RealInterfaceSetoid`；`RealEnhancedReal`，字段全部实值化），部分头条定理另有 Real 层逐 eps 直接复刻（`real_gibbs_inequality_eps`、`real_attention_is_gibbs` 等）；抽象定理签名向 setoid 实例的整体迁移（已有定理级试点两件，§10.2 第 1 项）、以及抽象陈述与 Real 层复刻之间的 statement-level 机器对齐仍为开放工作（逐字段/逐定理对照见附录 C，详情见 §9.2 与 §10.2）。 --- **Abstract (English)** This work reports the machine-checked formalization of the mathematical core of the Free Energy Principle (FEP), the exact bridge between softmax attention and Gibbs distributions, and constructive quantitative theorems for KV-cache eviction, top-k truncation, and Min-P truncation inside the ConstructiveWorld library. All proofs are carried out in pure constructive logic (zero Axioms, zero Admitted proof obligations, relying only on the Coq standard library) and share a common base of Cauchy reals, Boltzmann distributions, and KL divergence. The core contributions form three threads: (i) the closure of the temperature-parameterized maximum-entropy duality (Theorems 4.6a–4.6e), proving existence and uniqueness of the constrained entropy maximizer for each temperature parameter together with strict temperature–energy monotonicity, centered on the symmetric KL identity (β1−β2)(E2−E1) = KL(p2‖p1) + KL(p1‖p2); (ii) the exact total-variation (TV) identity for top-k truncation (Theorem 7.6, TV = tail_mass/Z_thermo) and the quantitative characterization of Min-P truncation (Theorem 8.9: dropped ≤ 1 − 1/|S|, a corollary of the entropy bound dropped ≤ 1 − e^{−S}), giving quantitative characterizations of truncation error rather than qualitative bookkeeping; (iii) a constructive mechanism for avoiding LPO, replacing the law of excluded middle by the weak trichotomy `real_weak_trich`, replacing “non-strict and non-converging” statements by per-eps slack, and showing that error accumulation is exactly eps (rather than |S|·eps) through a normalization argument. In addition, viewing the iteration of the softmax attention layer as a Markov chain, total-variation contraction and iterative convergence are machine-checked under a Doeblin minorization assumption (δ ∈ (0,1), kernel ≥ δ · stationary mass), with explicit geometric rate (1−δ)ⁿ: `attention_tv_contraction`, `attention_tv_iter_contraction`, and `attention_iterate_converges`, all closed with Qed. A recent library extension further machine-checks a genuinely more general two-point form of this family (`u_tv_contraction` / `u_tv_iter`: no stationarity, no detailed balance, no `transition_nonneg`, no non-negativity of μ, reference distribution only required to be normalized) together with an explicit Doeblin instantiation on bounded-logit softmax attention kernels (`bs_minorization` with δ* := e^{−2Δ/T}; explicit contraction rate (1 − e^{−2Δ/T})ⁿ via `bounded_softmax_tv_contraction` / `bounded_softmax_tv_iter`), all closed with Qed (see §5.5, Theorems 5.4–5.6). Supporting layers include the variational free-energy decomposition, the Gibbs inequality and equality condition, uniqueness of the Boltzmann distribution as the free-energy minimizer, the ELBO lower bound and tightness condition, the exact correspondence between softmax attention and the Gibbs distribution (at unit temperature, at arbitrary temperature, and via the scale–temperature duality `scale_temp_duality`: for every c > 0, softmax with logits scaled by 1/c equals softmax at temperature c, closing the logits-level shape of the Transformer 1/√d scaling, with √d coverage now closed at both layers: machine-checked witness instances for every square dimension d = k² at the abstract layer (`sqrt_witness_nat_sq` and `scale_dual_nat_sq_k`), a constructive square root for every d ≥ 0 at the Real layer, including non-square d (`real_sqrt_exists`), and an abstract-layer witness instantiation for every non-negative d (`sqrt_witness_exists_abstract`, module `UpDebtSqrtAbs`)); see §5.4.An identity-based control of the steady-state deviation caused by KV-cache eviction (whose Set-layer content is the triangle inequality; see §6.2, while the temperature–Lipschitz quantitative bounds are carried by Real-layer Theorems 6.1b/6.1c in §6.2.1), the majorization optimality of top-k truncation, and the decidability, non-emptiness, normalization (`minp_markov_kernel_normalized`), and monotonicity relative to the full softmax kernel of Min-P truncated sampling (see §8).Since `free_energy_kl_decomp` and `rlhf_free_energy_kl` instantiate the same free-energy–KL decomposition, this work shares one mathematical base with RLHF/DPO alignment objectives. We present the core theorem statements, outline proof strategies, compare with related formalization work, and explicitly declare current boundaries. **On instantiation (honest boundary)**: the headline theorems are stated over the real-number interface `RealInterfaceEnhanced` (with `Id` equality); the setoid counterparts of this interface are end-to-end instantiated on concrete Cauchy reals (`Real_RealInterfaceSetoid`,; `RealEnhancedReal`,, all fields filled with real-valued constructions), and several headline theorems additionally have direct Real-layer per-eps replicas (`real_gibbs_inequality_eps`, `real_attention_is_gibbs`, etc.). The wholesale migration of abstract theorem statements onto the setoid instances, and a machine-checked statement-level alignment between abstract statements and Real-layer replicas, remain open work (see Appendix C for the per-field/per-theorem comparison table; details in §9.2 and §10.2). ---

title: Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container
abstract: This paper explores consciousness as a causal puzzle. Where an investigation of water molecules examines their properties, this inquiry follows the relations that sustain a whirlpool. It shifts attention from identifying consciousness within the brain to tracing the causal organization that could sustain one subject's present and history. The tools are Occam's principle and subtraction. Place a body, an environment, and conditions for continued existence on the board, then remove the relations one by one. What ceases to be possible when a relation is removed? This paper calls the method of narrowing down necessary causal roles through such removal "proof by absence." The proposed linkage connects viability-related candidate competition, strong information discard, consequences, and continuation. Strong information discard means that incompatible losers irreversibly lose their standing to determine continuation at the same branch, not that their information is completely erased. The winner's consequences become the same system's conditions of continuation and influence subsequent candidate formation. A loser may remain as information without becoming realized history; a winner may disappear as information while its consequences remain effective. An engineering interpretation of death clarifies what viability constraints constrain: the conditions sustaining a specified organization and the boundary at which its continuation is lost. History thereby operates not only as a record, but as present conditions shaping subsequent possibilities. The convergence-point criterion traces the coupling among the unit whose candidates compete, the unit whose conditions change, and the unit that continues from those conditions. The internal reference point denotes the role through which carried consequences influence subsequent formation. Through correspondence with one present, the bearing of consequences, a single history, and internal reference, together with explanatory economy, the paper strongly infers that the system realizing this coupling constitutes the subjective container. Identifying necessary causal roles and identifying their realization with the subject are separate steps. The latter is not a deductive proof of experience or of the structure's uniqueness. The framework begins below human language, self-awareness, and deliberation. It hypothesizes that brains broadly and closely implement this loop and predicts shared functional organization across species. Comparisons with existing theories examine how their mechanisms connect to the same linkage. Appendix A develops artificial-system design conditions; Appendix B examines boundaries of realization through sleep, anesthesia, identity-state switching, and related cases. The remaining puzzle concerns qualia: through what mechanism does the inferred subject feel its perceptions? The framework directs this question toward perceptual processes participating in the formation of the present of a system that bears consequences and continues. It offers a starting hypothesis for an as-yet-unknown theory of perceptual information becoming an experienced event. This perspective paper grew from a puzzle pursued through dialogue with generative AI by a disability welfare worker outside academic consciousness research, after first learning about the hard problem. It presents causal reasoning without experimental validation. Its contribution is a proposed subject structure, criteria for comparison and testing, and a more concrete question about the emergence of felt experience.

title: RTR-IRPT : The Canonical Theory - A Constitutional Reconstruction of Physical Structure
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: RTR-IRPT (Relational Topological Reality — Irreducible Relay Persistence Theory) is an attempt to reconstruct physical structure from a deliberately minimal starting point: a single inseparable constitutional triad of State, Relation, and Self-reference, with no space, time, probability, metric, or physical constant assumed in advance. Every downstream structure — genealogy, admissibility, quotient/equivalence machinery, irreducibility, local Lorentz-type structure, a forced quadratic measurement law, spatial dimensionality as a measurable (not assumed) quantity, and conditional bridges toward electromagnetism, gravity, and matter representation — is required to be earned from these three primitives or explicitly flagged as open. This submission is the frozen Version 1.0 canonical statement of that program: eleven parts covering the constitutional foundations, admissibility and quotient theory, operational extension to three dimensions, Lorentz/Maxwell structure, quantum measurement architecture, gravity and the Einstein sector, matter/spin/charge, a Reality-Contact ledger of structural correspondences to known physics, and — critically — a complete, dedicated Open Walls and Falsification Map (Part X) that lists every claim the theory does not currently derive, each stated as a precise missing implication rather than smoothed over. What is established: genuine theorems and no-go results — including several proved by explicit countermodel rather than assertion — governing genealogical persistence, behavioral equivalence and quotienting, irreducibility, conditional Lorentz and Maxwell-equivalent structure, a forced quadratic measurement law within an earned phase sector (with several of its physical consequences, such as the vanishing of higher-order interference and a fixed negative sign for finite-relay dispersion, reducing to that single parent theorem rather than standing as independent successes), and a precise reduction of spatial dimensionality to one unresolved asymptotic constant. What is explicitly not established, and is named as such: unique realization from bare admissibility; strong (P2/P3) identity persistence; a universal propagation scale and its identification with c; a unique global spacetime geometry; global complex/Hilbert-space uniqueness; Born-rule realized frequencies as a dynamical theorem (as opposed to a measurement weight); electric charge identity and normalization; unique fermionic matter selection and spin-statistics; particle mass selection; Planck/action normalization; dimensionless coupling constants; and the numerical value of spatial dimensionality itself (d=3 is measurable within the framework but not forced by it). RTR-IRPT is presented as a rigorous, self-auditing foundational research program — not as a completed physical theory, and not as a claim of a new falsifiable prediction beyond known physics at this stage. Its central, load-bearing finding, arrived at independently across more than a dozen separate branches, is structural: a Constitution built only from relation and self-reference can produce shape, sign, symmetry, and order, but does not by itself supply numerical magnitude. Closing any of the walls listed in Part X requires either a new theorem from the existing primitives, or an honestly declared additional postulate — the theory explicitly forbids inventing an unstated selector to force closure.

title: Editorial: Multisensory integration: unveiling the complexities of perception
abstract: Every moment of waking life confronts the nervous system with a torrent of signals arriving simultaneously through eyes, ears, skin, nose, and the body's internal receptors. Making sense of such a multiplicity of inputs requires more than processing each channel in isolation: the brain must decide which signals belong together, weigh their relative reliability, and merge them into a single, actionable representation of the world. This is the work of multisensory integration, classically defined as the neural process by which information from different sensory modalities is combined to enhance the salience and reliability of the resulting percept (Stein & Meredith, 1993). Once thought to be confined to late, associative stages of a strictly hierarchical processing chain, multisensory interactions are now known to occur at multiple levels of the nervous system, from subcortical structures such as the superior colliculus to primary sensory cortices themselves (Driver & Noesselt, 2008).Multisensory integration is not simply additive: it involves flexible, context-dependent computations that can enhance, suppress, or reweight individual sensory inputs. A large body of psychophysical work has shown that this reweighting closely approximates statistically optimal cue combination, in which each sense is weighted according to its momentary reliability (Ernst & Banks, 2002;Alais & Burr, 2004). Phenomena such as the McGurk effect, in which lip movements alter the perceived identity of speech sounds (McGurk & MacDonald, 1976), and the sound-induced flash illusion (Shams et al., 2000), illustrate how profoundly cross-modal interactions can shape, and distort, conscious experience. Attention and top-down expectation further modulate when and how strongly these interactions occur (Talsma et al., 2010), while systematic crossmodal correspondences between, for instance, pitch and visual size or brightness reveal that the mapping between senses is far from arbitrary (Spence, 2011) a principle whose reach extends well beyond the laboratory, into applied domains such as consumer neuroscience (Bortolotti, 2025). The full expression of these integrative abilities is not present at birth but unfolds gradually over childhood, a protracted developmental trajectory that may offer a window of opportunity for early intervention in atypical sensory processing (Bremner et al., 2012). This Research Topic, Multisensory integration: unveiling the complexities of perception, was launched to bring together contributions that probe this flexibility from complementary angles: computational modeling of how signals are combined, psychophysical and electrophysiological investigation of cross-modal effects on perception and action, and applied work exploring how multisensory principles play out in naturalistic and developmental contexts. The collection brings together twelve published articles and two further contributions that have been accepted and are currently in production, for a total of fourteen contributions, spanning Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, Frontiers in Neuroscience, and Frontiers in Psychology, offering a timely snapshot of a field that continues to challenge the classical, hierarchical view of sensory processing.A recurring theme is the search for the computational rules that govern how the brain weighs and merges different sources of information. Billock et al. (2026) show that multisensory suppressive neurons, rather than being a mere nuisance for integration models, can implement a Bayesian-like, nonlinearly weighted combination of sensory inputs, offering a neurally grounded account of how statistically optimal integration might be instantiated at the single-cell level. Complementary evidence comes from touch: Allen and Goldreich (2026) demonstrate that humans optimally combine cutaneous and proprioceptive cues when judging object size, extending the logic of statistically optimal fusion beyond the classical audiovisual domain into haptic perception. At the interface between vision and touch, Umemura and Iwaki (2025) reveal that the perceived simultaneity of visual and haptic events is not fixed but is shaped by the contextual consistency of the stimuli, underscoring how integration windows are recalibrated online rather than hard-wired.A second group of articles examines how the information gathered from one modality shapes processing in another, and how these interactions unfold in time. Rizzuto et al. (2026) show that fixational eye movements, typically studied as a purely visual phenomenon, track the segmentation of auditory streams, providing a striking example of oculomotor signatures of auditory perceptual organization. In the domain of social perception, Toro et al. (2026) combine behavioral and ERP measures to demonstrate that contextual cues systematically shape facial emotion recognition, indicating that emotion perception is inherently an integrative, context-sensitive process rather than a modular readout of facial configuration alone. Moving to sensorimotor coupling, Zhao et al. (2025) report that the well-known action effect on perception is not modulated by cognitive load, suggesting a degree of automaticity and resource-independence in how action shapes perceptual outcomes. Finally, Adamski and Latka (2025) revisit the classic rod-and-frame illusion using virtual reality, offering a methodological update that reinterprets a decades-old visuo-vestibular phenomenon with modern immersive tools.Beyond laboratory psychophysics, several contributions situate multisensory integration within real-world or developmentally relevant settings. Huo et al. (2025) investigate how the duration and concentration of olfactory stimuli affect sleep-related arousal during fatigue driving, pointing to concrete safety applications for multisensory countermeasures against drowsiness. Shafique et al. (2025) ask whether spatialized audio enhances the construction of mental representations of space, a question with direct relevance for assistive technology and sensory-substitution devices. Sun et al. (2025) examine perception-action coupling during discriminative interceptive actions, clarifying how perceptual decisions and motor execution are jointly tuned in time-pressured tasks. On the developmental and clinical side, Ge et al. (2025) show that structured basketball training can improve sensory integration in Chinese children with moderate sensory integration challenges, offering encouraging evidence for embodied, play-based interventions.Closing the collection on a more theoretical note, Bortolotti et al. (2025) introduce the notion of supercomplexity to bridge aesthetics and cognition, proposing a conceptual framework in which the integration of multiple, sometimes conflicting, perceptual and cognitive dimensions underlies aesthetic experience itself. This contribution reminds us that multisensory integration is not confined to the combination of low-level sensory estimates but extends into higherorder domains such as value, meaning, and aesthetic appreciation.At the time of writing, the collection continues to grow: an original research contribution by Chen, Luo, Yang, and Li, examining how environmental cues shape human face-value perceptions, was accepted for publication in Frontiers in Psychology on 14 April 2026, and a further original research contribution by He and Zeng, on visual perception and information design in metro wayfinding systems, was accepted for publication in Frontiers in Psychology on 10 February 2026; both are currently in production within this Research Topic. We look forward to these additional papers, which will further extend the scope of the collection, and we will update our characterization of the Topic, including full bibliographic details, once their final versions are published.Taken together, the fourteen contributions in this Research Topic, twelve already published and two accepted and in production, llustrate that multisensory integration cannot be captured by a single mechanism or a single level of description. Optimal-cue-combination models, single-neuron nonlinearities, oculomotor and electrophysiological markers, developmental interventions, and theoretical frameworks bridging perception and aesthetics all contribute pieces of the same puzzle. The diversity of methods, computational modeling, psychophysics, ERP, virtual reality, and applied field studies,mirrors the diversity of contexts in which multisensory integration operates, from milliseconds-long neural computations to years-long developmental trajectories.Several open questions emerge from this body of work and point to promising directions for future research. How do the statistically optimal weighting principles identified in controlled psychophysical settings scale up to the noisy, dynamic conditions of everyday life, such as driving or social interaction? To what extent are the automaticity and resistance to cognitive load reported for some cross-modal effects a general property of multisensory processing, or are they specific to particular tasks and modalities? And how can insights from developmental interventions and technological applications, such as spatialized audio and virtual reality, be more systematically integrated with the computational and neural models that currently dominate the basic-science literature?

title: Free and Forgetful Come in Pairs ── A Roll Call of Adjunctions: Counting Hom Sets Checks the Correspondence, and One of Two Compactifications Is Not Even a Functor ── [Paper 246]
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Operations that add something and operations that throw something away appear again and again: free constructions, completions, localisations, compactifications. These come in pairs, except that not all of them do. Under the single word compactification stood a left adjoint and something that is not even a functor. No new mathematical theorem and no new law is claimed. Scope of this paper (scope note): no new mathematical theorem and no new law is claimed. That free functors are left adjoint to forgetful ones, that the Stone-Cech compactification is a left adjoint, that the one-point compactification is functorial only for proper maps, and that the algebraic closure has no universal property are all standard. No measured value is cited; every number is obtained by exhaustive enumeration. No general category theory is developed; only the definition of an adjunction is used and the adjoint functor theorem is not entered. No point-set topology is developed; one instance of a map that fails to extend is used. The axiom of choice is not discussed; existence is separated from uniqueness and nothing more. No ranking of value is attached to being an adjoint; it is not claimed that a construction without an adjoint is inferior. The relation to earlier papers. Paper 153 separated three stages of forgetting and exhibited evidence that a right adjoint is absent; this paper counts the paired side, the left adjoints. Paper 201 showed that complete is four different claims; Section 5 separates which of them carries an adjoint. Paper 113 showed that a module is a limit rather than a wall, the neighbouring notion on the same shelf. Paper 149 treated the functoriality of pullback and pushforward; this paper looks at when such a functor has a partner. Paper 179 showed that cannot be constructed has several roots; Section 6 is a fourth case, existing but not unique. The setting. Two operations are adjoint when, roughly, maps out of the object built by one correspond one to one with maps into the object left by the other. The shape is that an operation which adds something is paired with an operation which throws something away. This paper names the constructions that are not paired. First, the pairing can be checked with numbers. Homomorphisms from the free group on n generators into a group must number exactly the order raised to the n, since the adjunction turns that into choosing n elements freely. For the cyclic group of order six and the symmetric group on three letters the counts at n equal to one, two and three are 6, 36 and 216. For the dihedral group of order eight and the quaternion group they are 8, 64 and 512. The count does not depend on the structure at all; one group is commutative and the other is not, and both give 216. Seen from a free group the interior of the target is invisible and only the number of elements shows. Second, a non-free source gives no power. Counting homomorphisms from a cyclic group, that is the elements whose n-th power is the identity, gives six for the dihedral group and two for the quaternion group at n equal to two. Neither is a power of eight, and now the interior of the target does show: two groups of the same order returned different numbers. Here is the separator. A cyclic group is not free; it imposes a relation, and to the extent that a relation is imposed the structure of the target enters the answer. Free means carrying no relation at all. Third, this is the core of the paper. Embedding a space into a closed one is called compactification, and there are two. The one-point compactification adds a single point at infinity, turning the line into a circle. The Stone-Cech compactification adds as much as possible. Take the plain inclusion of an open interval into the line and ask whether it extends to the one-point compactifications. It does not. The point at infinity of the interval is approached from both ends, while the inclusion sends those two ends to interior points of the line, where the point at infinity of the line is not. One point would need two destinations. The one-point compactification is therefore not even a functor on continuous maps, and becomes one only when restricted to proper maps: before any question of adjointness the correspondence fails to carry maps. The Stone-Cech construction, by contrast, is a left adjoint. Fourth, completion is not an adjoint until the class of maps is fixed. The completion of a metric space is an adjoint for uniformly continuous maps and for Lipschitz maps, and is not one for merely continuous maps. The reason is simple: a continuous map need not send Cauchy sequences to Cauchy sequences, so there is nothing to extend it to, and uniform continuity is placed there precisely to guarantee that. Writing that completion is a free construction requires saying which category. Fifth, the algebraic closure is not an adjoint. Every field has one, and it has the same shape as a completion: add what is missing and close up. Yet no universal property holds, and a map out of it into an algebraically closed field is not unique. The algebraic closure of the rationals carries infinitely many automorphisms other than the identity. It exists and is not unique. Paper 179 separated three roots of cannot be constructed, and this is a fourth case: constructible, but with no canonical construction. Failing to be an adjoint is not a defect and the algebraic closure is a perfectly useful construction; what is said here is only that the single phrase free construction erases this difference. Closing. Constructions that add something split into three stages: those that do not carry maps, those that carry maps without a partner, and those that have one. The separator is likewise three-fold. Does it carry maps at all? If so, does it have a partner? If so, in which category? Free construction, completion and closure all look alike and differ in whether a partner exists. Whether one exists can be seen by counting Hom sets: whether the count is the order raised to a power, and nothing more. On the making of this work: The ideas and content of this work stem from the author's own considerations. Assistance from an AI (a large language model) was used for structuring, English translation, and checking the algebra. Any remaining errors or misinterpretations are solely the author's. Feedback and corrections are sincerely appreciated. ----- 体系には「余計なものを足す」操作と「捨てる」操作が何度も現れる——自由化、完備化、局所化、コンパクト化。これらは対になっている。ただし全部が対になっているわけではない。同じ「コンパクト化」という語の下に、左随伴であるものと、関手ですらないものが並んでいた。新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない。 本稿の射程(射程注記):新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない。自由関手が忘却関手の左随伴であること、ストーン=チェックのコンパクト化が左随伴であること、一点コンパクト化が固有写像に対してのみ関手的であること、代数的閉包が普遍性を持たないことは、いずれも標準的である。測定値を引かない——本稿の数はすべて全数え上げで得たものである。圏論の一般論を作らない——随伴の定義だけを使い、随伴関手定理には立ち入らない。位相空間論を論じない——使うのは延長できない写像の実例ひとつである。選択公理を論じない——存在と一意性を分けるだけである。「随伴であること」に価値の順序をつけない——随伴でない構成が劣っているとは主張しない。 既刊との関係。論文153 は忘却関手を三段に分け、右随伴が無いことの証拠を挙げた——本稿はその対になる側、すなわち左随伴のほうを数える。論文201 は「完備」が四つの別の主張だと示した——第5節はそのうちどれが随伴を持つかを分ける。論文113 は「モジュールは壁ではなく、極限である」と示した——同じ圏論の棚の、隣の概念である。論文149 は引き戻しと押し出しの関手性を扱った——本稿はその関手が対を持つ場合を見る。論文179 は「構成できない」に別根があると示した——第6節は存在するのに一意でないという第四の場合である。 設定。二つの操作が随伴であるとは、おおよそ、片方で作った対象からの写像と、元の対象からもう片方で落とした先への写像とが一対一に対応することを言う。「余計なものを足す」操作と「捨てる」操作が対になっているという形である。本稿は、対になっていない構成を名指す。 第一に、対になっていることは数で確かめられる。n 個の生成元を持つ自由群から群への準同型の個数は、随伴が正しければ相手の元を n 個自由に選ぶことと同じであり、位数の n 乗ちょうどでなければならない。位数 6 の巡回群と三次対称群では、n が 1、2、3 のとき 6、36、216 になる。位数 8 の二面体群と四元数群では 8、64、512 になる。個数が群の構造に一切依らない——可換かどうかが違うのに、どちらも 216 である。自由群から見ると、相手の中身が見えない。見えているのは元の個数だけである。 第二に、自由でない相手からは冪にならない。巡回群からの準同型、すなわち n 乗して単位元になる元を数えると、n が 2 のとき二面体群で 6、四元数群で 2 になる。位数 8 の冪ではない。そして今度は相手の中身が見えている——同じ位数の二つの群が、違う数を返した。分離子はここにある。巡回群は自由ではなく、関係式を課している。関係式を課した分だけ、相手の構造が答に効いてくる。「自由」とは、関係式が一つも無いことである。 第三に、これが本稿の芯である。空間を閉じた空間に埋め込む操作をコンパクト化といい、二つある。一点コンパクト化は無限遠に点を一つ足し、実数直線を円にする。ストーン=チェックのコンパクト化は可能な限り大きく足す。開区間から実数直線へのただの包含写像を取り、一点コンパクト化に延長できるかを調べると、できない。開区間の無限遠点は両端の両方から近づかれるのに、包含写像はその二つを実数直線の内点へ送り、実数直線の無限遠点はそこにない。一点に送りたいのに、行き先が二つある。したがって一点コンパクト化は、連続写像の圏の上で関手ですらない。関手になるのは固有写像に制限したときだけである。随伴かどうか以前に、対応が写像を運ばない。一方ストーン=チェックは左随伴である。 第四に、完備化は写像の種類を決めるまで随伴でない。距離空間の完備化は、一様連続写像を許せば随伴になり、リプシッツ写像でも随伴になり、連続写像だけを許すと随伴でなくなる。理由は簡単で、連続写像はコーシー列をコーシー列に送らないので、完備化へ延ばす先が決まらない。一様連続性は、まさにそれを保証するために置かれている。「完備化は自由構成である」と書くとき、どの圏の話かを書かなければならない。 第五に、代数的閉包は随伴ではない。体には代数的閉包が存在し、「余計なものを足して閉じる」という完備化とよく似た形をしている。ところが普遍性が成り立たず、代数閉体への写像が一意に決まらない。有理数体の代数的閉包には、恒等写像でない自己同型が無数にある。存在するのに、一意でない。論文179 は「構成できない」に三つの別根があると示したが、これは第四の場合である——構成できるが、標準的な構成が無い。随伴でないことは欠陥ではなく、代数的閉包は完全に有用な構成である。言うのは、「自由構成」という一語で括るとこの違いが消えるということだけである。 結び。「余計なものを足す」構成は、三段に分かれた。写像を運ばないもの、運ぶが対を持たないもの、対を持つもの。分離子も三段である。そもそも写像を運ぶか。運ぶとして、対を持つか。対を持つとして、どの圏でか。「自由構成」「完備化」「閉包」といった語は、どれも同じ形に見えて、対の有無が違う。対を持つかどうかは、Hom の個数を数えれば見える——位数の冪になるかどうか、それだけである。 作成にあたって:本稿の着想と内容は、著者自身の考察に基づくものです。文章の構成整理や英訳、数式の確認には AI(大規模言語モデル)の助力を得ました。最終的な内容の解釈や誤りがあれば、それらはすべて著者の責に帰します。お気づきの点があれば、ご教示いただければ幸いです。

title: A Consistency Core for Process Matrices, with an Exact Closed-Form Causal Witness for the Oreshkov-Costa-Brukner Process
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Process matrices describe correlations with no definite order of operations, and the property that sets a genuinely indefinite process apart from an ordinary mixture of ordered ones is called causal nonseparability. This paper gives a careful, self-contained account of why the whole framework hangs together consistently, across three levels at once, the level of plain probabilities, the level of quantum measurement rules, and the level of classical logical consistency. Its main practical result is an exact, written-out certificate that detects the indefiniteness of the canonical process by hand, replacing a numerical computer search with a formula a reader can check with pencil and paper. Working in a convenient basis in which the relevant bookkeeping operations act especially simply, the paper derives the certificate in closed form as the identity minus two specific order-sensitive terms. It shows that the two natural pieces of this certificate are well-behaved in the technical sense required, each with an explicit, exactly known set of values and an explicit proof of positivity written as a sum of squares. Evaluated on the canonical indefinite process, the certificate returns a specific negative number exactly, which is precisely the signal of indefiniteness. The paper then abstracts the construction into a general recipe, a theorem stating that any certificate of this shape is valid whenever a simple sum-of-squares condition holds on its two pieces. Alongside this it lays out, level by level, how the framework stays consistent, from the requirement that probabilities behave, through the quantum measurement rule, to the classical fixed-point picture in which a would-be paradoxical loop has, or fails to have, a unique consistent resolution. Every numbered result is also formally verified in a machine proof assistant, to the authors' knowledge the first such verification for this framework, with the correspondence to the formal statements collected in an appendix. The value of the paper is to turn what had been the output of an opaque numerical optimizer into a transparent, reusable, and independently machine-checked object that anyone can audit and build on. By exhibiting an exact certificate and a general recipe for producing more, it lowers the barrier to certifying indefinite causal order, and by verifying the whole consistency core in a proof assistant it supplies a dependable formal foundation for later work. The paper is modest about what it adds, presenting the physics of the canonical process as already known and offering instead an exact and verifiable rendering of it.

title: THE VEIL AND THE WALL: Theological Interpretation of Riemann Hypothesis and P versus NP
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Two millennium problems, one skeleton, one bit apart. The Riemann Hypothesis stands in the codex at the composite [⟀] · [⟀ T] · [Ξ₀]: field sealed, shape sealed, formal truth-string in terminal suspension, the suspension residing in an orientation-blind reader who stands on a line and cannot read the sign. P versus NP stands at the sibling composite [⟀] · [⟀ T] · [Ø₀]: the witnessed cost asymmetry sealed, the shape of the question sealed, the formal string a Grounded-Sealed Halt on a terrain whose native reflection fixes nothing, the halt residing in the absence of any place to stand. One holding has a line under it and one does not, and the entire difference between the two arcs reduces to that single bit of eigenstructure. This volume gathers the nine confessional essays written on the second problem, consolidates the codex's own theological reading of the first, and states the comparative ledger whole: the veil of direction against the veil of station, blindness against placelessness, the keys of the unseen against the encompassing negated to the smallest fragment, reliance against servanthood, and one Edge at which both answers are held where no verdict-side standpoint is or ever will be. A capstone section, seated in this second edition, then reads the one utterance both composites live on, la ilaha illa: the double negation both arcs execute, the halted affirmation at which the Riemann arc stands with a line under it, and the seat of chosen silence toward which the complexity terrain's geometry points, the walk made executable on the Riemann side by the fortified keystone. A closing section then makes the work standalone: Trisduction introduced in brief, from the root axioms through the three warrant axes to the kernel identity λ² = det(R), its orientation-blindness, and the three-state economy with its two terminal tokens; and both final verdicts stated whole, the Riemann composite through its eight-gate suspension and the located door on the multiplicative axis, and the complexity verdict in its two courts, the four-layer holding and the jurisdiction barrier under which the structural lean is the only determination available at any standpoint that exists, each compressed from its full treatment and cited internally. Every mathematical result touched is classical and belongs to its authors. Every theological identification is a correspondence of shape at premise grade, carried out of band, load-bearing on nothing in any verdict, and settling no mathematical question in either direction. The contribution is an arrangement, and an arrangement is not a mass. La ilaha, illa: Riemann halts at the affirmation, standing on the line it cannot read. One step beyond, the line folds to the point no one occupies, and the silence that follows is already seated [.]

title: Operator-Theoretic and Computational Realizations of the Riemann Hypothesis Expanded
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Operator-Theoretic and Computational Realizations of the Riemann Hypothesis Expanded Driven by Dean Kulik July 2026 Introduction to the Spectral Architecture and Computational Ontology The analytic infrastructure surrounding the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) has progressively migrated from classical bounds in complex analysis toward profound operator-theoretic formalisms. For over a century, the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture hypothesized that the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, , correspond precisely to the spectrum of a self-adjoint operator. This correspondence would guarantee, through the application of the spectral theorem, that all such zeros must lie exactly on the critical line defined by . While historically treated as an elegant heuristic to explain the apparent collinearity of the zeros, modern advancements at the intersection of noncommutative geometry, spectral triples, and high-precision numerical computation have materialized this hypothetical operator into a rigorously defined, computationally verifiable mathematical object. Recent developments have catalyzed a paradigm shift, establishing that verifying the Riemann Hypothesis is mathematically equivalent to proving the strict positive semidefiniteness of a specific infinite-dimensional quadratic form: the Weil explicit formula evaluated as a Gram matrix. This framework inherently shifts the burden of proof. The objective of modern RH research is no longer the isolated localization of individual zeros in the complex plane, but rather the structural demonstration that a naturally arising geometric operator—constructed entirely from discrete prime numbers and the continuous archimedean Gamma factor—maintains strict positivity in its infinite-dimensional continuum limit. The deepest revelation of this modern framework lies in its computational ontology. The explicit formula splits cleanly into two fundamental topological shapes. The first is a discrete sum over primes governed by the von Mangoldt function, acting as an "accumulate" mechanism that gathers arithmetic data. The second is a continuous integral over the archimedean factor governed by the digamma function, acting as a "bloom" mechanism that smooths the data. These components do not merely exist side-by-side in a static identity; they dynamically interleave into a single Hankel matrix factorization, where the discrete prime sum provides the raw, countable data, and the continuous archimedean kernel serves as the smooth instruction set or carrier wave. Together, they produce a sequence of moments that define a Gaussian-weighted zero-counting measure. This synthesis proves that computation is not merely a post-hoc tool utilized to check mathematics; in this highly specific context, the computation is the mathematics. The static result of the proof is merely a shadow of the dynamical system, functioning analogously to a logical processor running a 1-bit data stream of primes through a 4-bit instruction set of Gamma-factor symmetries to output the critical line. Noncommutative Geometry and the Adele Class Space The rigorous formulation of this spectral operator finds its geometric footing in the noncommutative geometry of the adele class space. The global topology required to simultaneously capture the discrete, localized behavior of prime numbers and the continuous, global behavior of the real numbers necessitates a unified mathematical space. The adele ring, denoted as over the rational numbers , is constructed as the restricted direct product of all -adic completions alongside the real archimedean completion . The critical geometric space for analyzing the Riemann zeta function is the adele class space, defined as the quotient space , where is a finite set of places of (including the archimedean place at infinity), and represents the diagonal action of the group generated by the primes in the set . This semilocal space elegantly resolves singular measure-theoretic issues that are present in the full adele class space, primarily because the multiplicative and additive Haar measures are no longer mutually singular under this specific quotient construction. Alain Connes' pioneering work on this space established a fundamental trace formula that perfectly recovers the Riemann-Weil explicit formula. Within this noncommutative geometric setting, there is a natural action of the idele class group, given by . Connes' trace formula acts as a mathematical bridge between two distinct realms: the spectral side, which corresponds to the contributions from the zeros of -functions with Grössencharakter, and the geometric side, which corresponds to the contributions from the places of (representing the prime numbers). Consequently, the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture is realized not as an isolated functional analytic curiosity, but as a fundamental consequence of the geometry of the adele class space and the scaling actions upon it. The Guinand-Weil Explicit Formula and Analytical Duality To translate this noncommutative geometric reality into an evaluable operator, the framework relies upon the Guinand-Weil explicit formula. This is an intricate harmonic identity that establishes a profound, exact duality between the prime numbers and the complex zeros of the Riemann zeta function. The explicit formula mathematically balances the contributions of the quantum-like spectrum of zeros against the discrete arithmetic of the prime powers. Formally, the explicit formula is evaluated against a suitably smooth, even test function that is holomorphic in a specified strip in the complex plane and satisfies stringent decay conditions. Typically, these test functions are chosen from the Paley-Wiener space or the Schwartz space , ensuring that their Fourier and Mellin transforms possess the necessary compact support or exponential decay to guarantee absolute convergence. The identity inherently equates the sum of the transform of the test function, evaluated at the nontrivial zeros, to a series of arithmetic and continuous distributions. The archimedean distribution represents the place at infinity, requiring sophisticated numerical quadrature to evaluate the highly continuous, singular digamma component. The immense power of this formula lies in its status as an absolute identity. Because the explicit formula equates the arithmetic geometric components to the spectral sum over the zeros, it inherently encodes the global constraints of the zeta function into an evaluable mathematical sum. If the Riemann Hypothesis holds true, all nontrivial zeros lie on the critical line, meaning they must take the exact form where the ordinate is strictly real. Positivity Criteria: From Weil to Bombieri and Lagarias André Weil utilized the inherent duality of the explicit formula to demonstrate a profound equivalence: the Riemann Hypothesis is mathematically equivalent to the positive semidefiniteness of a specific infinite-dimensional quadratic form, now universally known as the Weil form. By treating the explicit formula as a distribution applied to convolution products of test functions (specifically ), Weil showed that for all nontrivial correspondences. This conceptual leap transitioned the analytic problem of root-finding in the complex plane into a pure algebraic problem of operator positivity. This positivity framework was significantly expanded decades later by Xian-Jin Li, who formulated a criterion stating that the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to the strict non-negativity of a specific sequence of numbers for all positive integers . Li's sequence is derived directly from the Taylor expansion of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Riemann xi-function, evaluated at the critical point : Expressed dynamically in terms of the complex zeros , this sequence takes the elegant sum form . If any zero were to possess a real part strictly less than (and by symmetry, one greater than ), the exponential growth of the off-line components would eventually force a term into negative territory, violating the criterion. Enrico Bombieri and Jeffrey C. Lagarias subsequently provided a critical arithmetic interpretation of Li's sequence, binding it firmly back to the Weil explicitly formula. They observed a fundamental algebraic identity governing the structure of these specific polynomial terms : By applying this algebraic identity, Bombieri and Lagarias proved that Li's criterion is not an isolated phenomenon specific solely to the Riemann zeta function, but rather a generalized consequence of an arbitrary multiset of complex numbers operating under specific conjugation symmetries. Furthermore, they demonstrated that a certain analytical truncation of the sequence can be expressed exactly as Weil's explicit formula. The positivity of these specific arithmetic truncations implies the Riemann Hypothesis, effectively bridging the continuous, infinite-dimensional operator theory with highly computable, discrete algebraic sequences. title: Reframing thymic epithelial tumors through single-cell transcriptomics: a narrative review
abstract: Background and Objective: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare neoplasms originating from thymic epithelial cells (TECs). They exhibit histological, molecular, and immunological diversity shaped by aberrant interactions between neoplastic TECs and immune cells. World Health Organization (WHO) histological classification effectively captures their clinicopathological features, whereas inter- and intra-subtype heterogeneity persists. In this point, single-cell transcriptomics is well-suited to resolve cellular heterogeneity in TETs. This narrative review synthesizes findings from recent single-cell studies that illuminate epithelial subpopulations, intra-tumoral immune landscape, and disease-specific aberrations such as myasthenia gravis (MG)-associated phenotypes in TETs. Methods: We conducted a focused narrative review on three key studies that applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to primary human TETs. Key Content and Findings: Single-cell analyses identified a distinct TEC subpopulation ectopically expressing neuromuscular antigens, termed neuromuscular medullary TECs (nmTECs), in MG-associated thymomas, implicating aberrant antigen presentation and immune cell recruitment in autoantibody production. Other studies delineated tumor epithelial programs that shape the immune microenvironment, linking TEC transcriptional identities to the persistence of immature T-cells or dominance of mature T-cells. Bioinformatic approaches of ligand-receptor networks supported pathogenic crosstalk between neoplastic TECs and immune cells. Notably, independent groups converged on functionally oriented classifications that align across studies, stratifying TETs by epithelial lineage programs and immune composition with correspondence to biological behavior and prognosis. Conclusions: Single-cell approaches have revealed TET heterogeneity encompassing abnormal epithelial cell states, immune development trajectories, and autoimmune-associated molecular programs with high resolution. The ongoing accumulation of single-cell transcriptomics datasets would refine a cell-centric framework for TET classification and pathogenesis, while also deepening insight into normal TEC biology.

title: 生命社会学原理——基于自相似性原理的社会系统论 Life Sociology: A Social Systems Theory Based on the Self-Similarity Principle
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper applies the Self-Similarity Principle to the social sciences, demonstrating that society is a life system—not metaphorically, but in the strict ontological sense. Just as a biological organism maintains its existence through the preservation of internal proportional relationships, a society maintains its stability through the preservation of its core structural ratios. The paper establishes a systematic correspondence between biological and social structures: · Brain ↔ Central government: strategic decision-making and macro-regulation· Limbs ↔ Primary industry and defense: resource acquisition and security· Digestive system ↔ Secondary industry: material transformation and production· Circulatory system ↔ Transportation: logistics and energy distribution· Nervous system ↔ Communication networks: information transmission and coordination· Immune system ↔ Healthcare and public security: defense and internal purification Beyond physiological structures, the paper extends the correspondence to psychological dimensions: · Self-consciousness ↔ Ideology: a society's awareness of "who we are"· Memory ↔ Cultural tradition: collective experience shaping present identity Based on this self-similarity between biological and social life, the paper reinterprets fundamental questions in political economy: · Plan and Market: They are not opposed systems but hierarchical divisions of labor—the brain (central government) handles macro-planning, while organs (markets) handle micro-regulation. The failure of historical planned economies is diagnosed as a feedback loop deficiency: the "brain" attempted to regulate individual cells, exceeding its functional capacity. As information technology advances, the boundary between plan and market shifts dynamically.· Public and Private Ownership: Ownership is the unity of static property rights and dynamic usage rights. Private property always contains a "public component" (legal constraints, taxation, social responsibility), and this public component increases with social development. Public property, without proper oversight, risks privatization by vested interests—analogous to cellular cancerization.· Socialism and Capitalism: Socialism is a society with clear self-consciousness—it knows "who we are" and pursues balanced, sustainable development. Capitalism is a desire-driven system where capital's will overrides collective self-awareness, leading to systemic imbalance. A society that loses its ideological self-consciousness through uncontrolled openness becomes a "living corpse"—physiologically functioning but psychologically hollow. The paper further proposes a quantitative framework for social analysis: · Broken-symmetry degree D(t) for measuring societal deviation from healthy baseline ratios· Critical threshold Dc for early warning of systemic crisis· Four-step analytical procedure: identify system parameters → discover core ratios → track symmetry-breaking → determine critical thresholds The evolutionary direction of social life is increasing orderliness (有序化), ultimately pointing toward the ideal of a harmonious society (大同世界)—not as a utopian fantasy, but as the natural state of a highly evolved, healthy social organism maintaining dynamic equilibrium across all its subsystems. This paper applies the Self-Similarity Principle established in the author's earlier collection The Self-Similarity Principle: A Unified Theory of Existence, Change, and Knowledge to the social sciences, extending the framework from physics and philosophy into political economy. --- 本文基于自相似性原理,系统论证社会是一个生命系统——这不是比喻,而是严格的存在论判断。正如生物有机体通过维持内部比例关系来保持存在,社会也通过维持其核心结构比例来保持稳定。 论文建立了生物结构与社会结构的系统对应: · 大脑 ↔ 中央政府:战略决策与宏观调控· 四肢 ↔ 第一产业与国防:资源获取与安全保障· 消化系统 ↔ 第二产业:物质转化与生产制造· 循环系统 ↔ 交通运输:物资流通与能量分配· 神经系统 ↔ 通讯网络:信息传递与协调控制· 免疫系统 ↔ 医疗卫生与安全机构:防御外敌与清除内患 在生理结构之外,论文将对应延伸到心理维度: · 自我意识 ↔ 意识形态:社会对“我们是谁”的认知· 记忆 ↔ 文化传统:集体经验塑造当下身份 基于这一生物生命与社会生命的自相似性,论文重新阐释政治经济学的根本问题: · 计划与市场:不是对立体制,而是层次分工——大脑(中央)管宏观计划,器官(市场)管微观调节。计划经济的根本失败在于反馈闭环缺失:“大脑”越层试图调控每个细胞,超出其功能边界。随着信息技术发展,计划与市场的边界动态变化。· 公有制与私有制:所有制是静态所有权与动态运用权的统一。私有财产始终含有“公有成分”(法律约束、税收调节、社会责任),该成分随社会有序化而递增。公有财产若缺乏有效监督,面临被小团体窃取的风险——相当于细胞癌变。· 社会主义与资本主义:社会主义是具有清晰自我意识的社会——知道“我们是谁”,追求平衡可持续发展。资本主义是欲望驱动的失控系统,资本意志凌驾于集体自我意识之上。在对外开放中丧失意识形态自我意识的社会,将成为“行尸走肉”——生理运转但心理空洞。 论文进一步提出社会分析的量化框架: · 破缺度 D(t):衡量社会偏离健康基线比例的程度· 临界阈值 Dc:系统性危机的预警指标· 四步分析程序:识别系统参数 → 发现核心比例 → 追踪破缺 → 判读阈值 社会生命的进化方向是高度有序化,最终指向大同世界的理想——不是乌托邦幻想,而是高度进化、健康的社会有机体在各子系统间维持动态平衡的自然状态。 本文是作者此前十三篇论文集《自相似性原理:存在、变化与知识的统一理论》在社会科学领域的应用延伸,将该框架从物理学与哲学拓展至政治经济学

title: War, Power, and Society: the Dynamics and Consequences of the Kiriji War in Yorubaland
abstract: The collapse of the Oyo Empire in the early nineteenth century created a profound political vacuum in Yorubaland, facilitating the rise of Ibadan as a dominant military and political power. This ascendancy was consolidated by Ibadan’s victory over the Fulani forces at the Battle of Osogbo in 1840. However, Ibadan’s expanding influence, characterized by centralized authority and increasingly coercive modes of control, generated widespread resistance among other Yoruba polities, culminating in the Kiriji (Ekiti-Parapo) War of the late nineteenth century. This study examines the Kiriji War as a critical turning point in the political and socio-cultural transformation of Yorubaland in present-day southwestern Nigeria. The paper analyzes Ibadan’s military and administrative strategies, the structural and immediate causes of the conflict, and the strategic importance of Igbajo and Imesi-Ile as the principal military encampments of the Ibadan and Ekiti-Parapo forces, respectively. It further explores the broader political, social, and cultural consequences of the war, particularly its role in redefining inter-polity relations and regional identities. Methodologically, the study adopts a historical research design that integrates primary and secondary sources. Primary data were drawn from Key Informant Interviews with local historians and community stakeholders, oral testimonies from selected residents, and archival materials—including colonial ordinances, intelligence reports, correspondence, and official gazettes—sourced from the National Archives, Ibadan, and the Lagos State Records and Archives Bureau. These were complemented by relevant scholarly literature, government publications, and photographic documentation of historically significant sites. The findings demonstrate that Ibadan’s post-Oyo dominance, sustained through military superiority and political coercion, provoked sustained opposition rooted in struggles over autonomy, territorial control, and access to resources. The strategic selection of Igbajo and Imesi-Ile reflected both geographic advantage and political symbolism. Despite its prolonged violence and devastation, the Kiriji War fostered new forms of socio-cultural interaction, strengthened regional consciousness, and encouraged cooperation among previously rival Yoruba communities. Politically, the conflict contributed to the gradual reconfiguration and partial unification of Yoruba polities. The study concludes that the Kiriji War, while destructive, played a significant role in shaping political authority, socio-cultural integration, and collective identity in nineteenth-century Yorubaland.
